category: tcp tunnel software with a public relay

free_tier.stated: Global Socket allows two workstations on different private networks to communicate with each other. Through firewalls and through NAT - like there is no firewall.

egress.terms: No byte, port or time limit is published on the project page; the relay is volunteer-run and carries no price.; ingress: tcp

chaining: TCP ingress for a VM without a card.

limits.value: No quota is published, so an unpublished tolerance on a volunteer relay is what fails at 1 TiB/month. TCP only: a WireGuard peer cannot be reached through it.

binding_note: No quota is published, so an unpublished tolerance on a volunteer relay is what fails at 1 TiB/month. TCP only: a WireGuard peer cannot be reached through it.

identity_cost.detail: a shared secret string is the only credential: 'gsocket -s ExampleSecretChangeMe /usr/sbin/sshd -D'.

reliability_note: Shared secret, no account: anyone holding the secret reaches the service, and the relay operator can see connection metadata.
confidence_note: No allowance is published at all, so the free relay is a lead rather than a measured number.

evidence.proved: 'two workstations on different private networks to communicate'; SSH example over the relay; 'SRP-AES-256-CBC-SHA-End2End'

notes: A free public relay with no account and end-to-end encryption, carrying TCP only. Closest thing here to a no-identity TCP ingress, which is why it is worth a measurement even though it is not UDP.

extras.volume_stated: No byte, port or time limit is published on the project page; the relay is volunteer-run and carries no price.
